prompt: Will California enact SB 951 by September 30, requiring employers to report AI-driven mass layoffs and decisions to stop hiring for specific jobs—including the affected roles, automated work, and AI technology used—for public state summaries?
editorial_note: We picked this because SB 951 would extend California's worker-notice system beyond ordinary layoff counts. Employers would have to identify mass layoffs materially driven by AI, report decisions to stop hiring for particular roles because of automation, describe the affected work and technology, and give the state information it would summarize publicly.

evidence_brief.fact: As of August 24, 2026, SB 951 was an active bill in the Assembly floor process after being ordered to third reading on August 21.
evidence_brief.source: California Legislative Information, official SB 951 status

evidence_brief.fact: Existing Cal/WARN law generally requires 60 days' notice for a covered mass layoff, relocation, or termination. SB 951 would add disclosures when that action is caused in whole or substantial part by AI or other automated technology, including affected occupations, automated job functions, and the type of technology responsible.
evidence_brief.source: California Legislative Counsel's Digest and proposed Labor Code section 1401(d)

evidence_brief.fact: SB 951 would also require a technology hiring disruption notice when an employer stops hiring or contracting for a particular position in whole or substantial part because of AI or automation. The state Employment Development Department would publish summaries of reported displacement.
evidence_brief.source: California Legislative Counsel's Digest and proposed Labor Code section 1402.7

evidence_brief.fact: California's 2026 calendar sets August 31 as the last day for each house to pass bills and September 30 as the governor's deadline to sign or veto qualifying bills.

A Stanford Digital Economy Lab analysis using ADP payroll data reported that employment among workers ages 22 to 25 in highly AI-exposed occupations was about 19% below a comparison path by June 2026, with the divergence operating mainly through reduced hiring rather than separations.
evidence_brief.source: Stanford Digital Economy Lab, Canaries in the Coal Mine? August 2026 update
evidence_brief.limitation: The researchers describe these as early descriptive indicators, not causal estimates of AI's effect.

resolution_clarity.source_of_truth: California Legislative Information official SB 951 status and chaptered bill text
resolution_criteria: Resolves YES only if California's official bill record lists SB 951 as Chaptered on or before September 30, 2026.
The chaptered text must require disclosure when a Cal/WARN-covered mass layoff is caused in whole or in substantial part by AI or other automated technology.
The chaptered text must require reporting when an employer stops hiring or contracting for specific positions in whole or in substantial part because of AI or automation.
The required reports must identify the affected roles or job functions and the AI or automated technology responsible, and the state must publish summaries of the reported displacement.
Resolves NO if SB 951 is vetoed, is not chaptered by the deadline, or any of these substantive requirements is removed. Cosmetic wording changes do not affect resolution.
